N-Acetylcysteine (NAC) Parvolex / Paradote 
* Use the Paracetamol Treatment Nomogram to establish need for antidote 
* If a high dosage is suspected, rather give the antidote to the patient 
* DO NOT withhold even if the ingestion was 48-72hrs prior to presentation 
* Administer NAC as follows (old regimen): 
•
150mg/kg in 200ml 5% Dextrose IV over 1 hour followed by 
•
50mg/kg in 500ml 5% Dextrose IV over 4 hours followed by 
•
100mg/kg in 1L 5% Dextrose IV over 16 hours 
* Preferred dosing regimen (SNAP Protocol) – NB Inform admitting doctor to continue this regimen! 
•
100mg/kg in 200ml 5% Dextrose IV over 2 hours followed by 
•
200mg/kg in 1 L 5% Dextrose IV over 10 hours 
 
Start treatment as soon as possible 
if indicated, 
preferably < 8hrs post-ingestion 
IF IN DOUBT, GIVE NAC 
DISPOSITION 
Int Med Referral 
PARACETAMOL OVERDOSE 
TOXIC DOSE 
150mg/kg or > 10g in adults 
 
INITIAL ASSESSMENT & MANAGEMENT 
* Assess and support ABC’s 
* Monitor glucose 
* Attempt to quantify the amount ingested & of any co-ingestants 
* Establish a timeframe from the time of ingestion to presentation 
* Presentation < 1 hour from ingestion 
• Activated charcoal 50g PO (not via NGT) 
* ECG – look for signs of co-ingestants e.g. prolonged QT 
* Laboratory investigations 
• Blood gas, U&E, salicylate level 
• Paracetamol levels (provided  4 hours post ingestion) 
• No need for AST/ALT/INR unless > 12 hours post ingestion 
 
**Refer to Protocol: General management principles of a poisoned/overdose patient** 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
NAC CAUTIONS/SIDE-EFFECTS – Less common with SNAP Protocol 
*Anaphylaxis 
*Vomiting 
*Separate IV infusion as may be inactivated by other medications 
PREGNANCY 
*Paracetamol crosses the placenta 
*Administer NAC as above 
HIGH RISK PATIENTS 
*Hypotensive 
*Pre-existing liver dysfunction e.g. alcoholic 
*Elderly 

 
 
 
 
Dr R Gihwala CMJAH Emergency Department June 2020 

 
 
EXPLANATION 
* 
If recipient presents after 72 hours and has significant exposure please consult HIV 
doctor regarding initiating nPEP 
** HIV Tests: HIV rapid takes 30minutes. If positive then source has HIV, but if 
negative would recommend 4th generation ELISA (window period of 15-20days) 
Def.: 
Source: the person whom you obtained injury from. 
Recipient: the person who is injured 
POST EXPOSURE PROPHYLAXIS: NON-OCCUPATIONAL 
 
FOLLOWING CIRCUMSTANCES MAY ARISE: 
• 
Sexual exposure/’Burst condom’ 
• 
Assault of multiple persons with exposure to blood from multiple sources, e.g. single weapon 
used. 
• 
Human bite 
• 
Contact sports with blood exposure 
• 
Sharing of needles 
• 
Blood coming in contact with mucous membranes or non-intact skin
